sections.title: 3.1 Service Registration
sections.text_preview:
This feature is associated with the registration of resource and service information of each CDN to its SR. The use case for this feature is shown in Figure 2.

![](images/bc0217ebeedbf6b2ca07fc20e367

sections.title: 3.1.1 Actors
sections.text_preview:
WS: Publishes its resource and service information to the SR.

SR: Registers available local resources at the CDN provider and updates them.

Mediator: Collects up-to-date resource information from SR

sections.title: 3.1.2 Trigger
sections.text_preview: Service registration is triggered when either one of the following occurs: (a) resources are available as a provider starts operating; (b) previously registered resource information needs to be update

sections.title: 3.1.3 Preconditions
sections.text_preview: Available local resources of a CDN provider are detected along with their service information such as CPU, storage, upload and download rate, etc. These resources could be provisioned and reserved to

sections.title: 3.1.4 Postconditions
sections.text_preview: Resources are registered in the service registry and being updated in a regular basis.

sections.title: 3.1.5 Stimulus/Response Sequences
sections.text_preview:
1. Each CDN Web server publishes resource and service information.

2. If it is a new resource, its service information is registered in the SR with a new resource ID. Resource ID counter is increment

sections.title: 3.1.6 Exceptions
sections.text_preview: If a resource fails, its service information is removed from SR and the resource ID counter is decremented.

sections.title: 3.1.7 Functional Requirements
sections.text_preview:
REQ-1: The format for service information description is defined

REQ-2: The interaction protocol between Web Server-SR, SR-mediator is defined.

REQ-3: Resource provisioning, delegation and reservati

sections.title: 3.2 Request Initiation to Trigger Peering
sections.text_preview:
This feature relates to the initialization of peering between CDNs. The use case for this feature is shown in Figure 3.

![](images/333af7ad0710fc2d69c2a15becd011396aeae8c089164f4981680d4b1904aeab.jpg

sections.title: 3.2.1 Actors
sections.text_preview:
End-user: Requests for content.

Mediator: Receives initiation request from WS to trigger peering.

sections.title: 3.2.2 Trigger
sections.text_preview: It is invoked when a (primary) CDN realizes that it cannot handle a part of the workload on its WS(s). The triggering condition considers the expected and unexpected load increases in the initiating (

sections.title: 3.2.3 Preconditions
sections.text_preview: Exceptional circumstances such as flash crowds have occurred to place unanticipated load on CDN WSs.

sections.title: 3.2.4 Postconditions
sections.text_preview: An initialization request is sent to the mediator to trigger peering.

sections.title: 3.2.5 Stimulus/Response Sequences
sections.text_preview:
1. End users request for content from CDN WSs.

2. Flash crowds occurred due to a sudden burst in traffic.

3. Hotspot is generated and provider is unable to handle excess load on its WSs.

4. WS send

sections.title: 3.2.6 Exceptions
sections.text_preview: If the user requests experience service timeout (threshold), initiation request is cancelled.

sections.title: 3.2.7 Functional Requirements
sections.text_preview:
REQ-1: Malicious requests are detected and rejected.

REQ-2: Web servers have already replicated necessary content.

REQ-3: Both anticipated and unanticipated user requests (traffic) are considered.

sections.title: 3.3 Mediator Invokes Creation of Negotiated Relationship
sections.text_preview:
On receipt of the initialization request to trigger peering, the mediator of the primary CDN invokes negotiation. Figure 4 shows use case for this feature.

![](images/9461f7909f362b3fc16094defb18113f

sections.title: 3.3.1 Actors
sections.text_preview:
SR: Sends resource and access information.

PR: Sends policy information for establishing negotiated relationships.

PA: Receives service requirements from the mediator.

sections.title: 3.3.2 Trigger
sections.text_preview: Upon receiving the initialization request to trigger peering, the mediator generates service requirements and passes it to local PA.

sections.title: 3.3.3 Preconditions
sections.text_preview: Initialization request is received.

sections.title: 3.3.4 Postconditions
sections.text_preview: Service requirements are generated and they are sent to the local PA.

sections.title: 3.3.5 Stimulus/Response Sequences
sections.text_preview:
1. An initialization request to activate peering is received by the mediator.

2. The mediator instance obtains resource and access information from the SR and policy information from PR to establish

sections.title: 3.3.6 Exceptions
sections.text_preview: If the user requests can not be accepted according the provider policies, service requirements are not passed to the local PA.

sections.title: 3.3.7 Functional Requirements
sections.text_preview:

REQ-2: Mediator-SR, mediator-PR, mediator-PA interaction protocols are defined.

REQ-3: Mediator works in conjunction with the PA to establish ne

sections.title: 3.4 Resource Discovery through PA
sections.text_preview: The PA of a given primary CDN negotiates with PAs of the peers to perform external resource discovery. Figure 5 shows the use case related to this feature.

sections.title: 3.4.1 Actors
sections.text_preview:
External PA: Negotiates with the PA of the primary CDN.

PR: Receives negotiated policies from the local PA.

sections.title: 3.4.2 Trigger
sections.text_preview: Local PA communicates with the PAs of peers to discover external resources.

sections.title: 3.4.3 Preconditions
sections.text_preview: Service requirements are received from the mediator.

sections.title: 3.4.4 Postconditions
sections.text_preview: Negotiation is performed and a peering arrangement is established through inter-PA communications.

sections.title: 3.4.5 Stimulus/Response Sequences
